summary: Iraq has closed multiple border crossings with Iran following Saudi accusations that Iranian-backed militias in Iraq attacked the East-West pipeline. Iran acknowledges obtaining Chinese satellite imagery of a U.S. base in Jordan prior to a deadly July missile strike. Heavy clashes erupt in southeastern Iran between security forces and Baluchi separatists, while a sanctioned Iranian supertanker breaches a U.S. naval blockade.
key_points: Iraq closed the Shalamcheh, Sheeb, and Mandali border crossings with Iran after Saudi Arabia blamed Iraqi-based drones for a pipeline attack, confirmed by Khuzestan's deputy governor. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/80749)
Saudi Foreign Ministry officially stated drones targeting the East-West pipeline originated from Iraq. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/7076)
U.S. officials say Iran used high-resolution Chinese satellite imagery of a Jordanian base before a July 17 ballistic missile strike that killed three American troops. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/7085)

Iran's President Pezeshkian announced a Hormuz transit agreement with Oman to be signed Monday in Muscat with Gulf Arab states present, including those hosting U.S. forces. (Source: @mamlekate/104458)
Three IRGC members were killed in Saravan during heavy clashes with Sunni Baluchi separatists near the Pakistan border. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/80760)
The OFAC-sanctioned supertanker Karina, carrying 22 million barrels of Iranian crude, passed through the U.S. naval blockade into the Gulf of Oman. (Source: @kianmeli1/91842)

Bahrain declared it will not attend any joint meetings with Iran until full diplomatic relations are restored, demanding cessation of attacks and respect for sovereignty. (Source: @SharghDaily/183319)
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman said the U.S. admitted the Lamerd attack used prohibited missiles, with four missiles striking a city of 30,000 within 35 seconds. (Source: @SharghDaily/183324)

sections.executive_summary: Iraq has shut key border crossings with Iran after Saudi Arabia attributed a pipeline attack to Iranian-backed militias operating from Iraqi territory. U.S. officials revealed Iran obtained Chinese satellite imagery of a Jordan base before a deadly July missile strike. Simultaneously, heavy fighting erupted in Iran's Saravan region, and a sanctioned Iranian supertanker evaded a U.S. naval blockade.

points: Iran's President Pezeshkian, visiting India, described U.S. pressure as having reached a 'difficult and dangerous' stage and called for 'operational cooperation' among BRICS members to counter it. (Source: @VahidOnline/78335)

Foreign Ministry spokesman Baqaei stated the U.S. admitted the Lamerd attack was carried out with prohibited missiles, noting four missiles hit a 30,000-population city within 35 seconds, proving the crime's deliberate nature. (Source: @SharghDaily/183324)

Iran's Foreign Ministry announced it will present results of Hormuz transit negotiations with Oman at a meeting of Gulf littoral states, insisting its nuclear program is peaceful and that erroneous IAEA reports justify aggression. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/391138)
IRGC Commander Ahmad Vahidi met with Iranian Army Chief Amir Hatami, signaling high-level military coordination. (Source: @asafroz/53359)

Heavy clashes broke out in Saravan, southeastern Iran near the Pakistan border, between Sunni Baluchi separatists and local security forces, resulting in three IRGC fatalities. (Source: @asafroz/53344, @rodast_omiddana/80760)

The sanctioned supertanker Karina (IMO 9240512), which transported at least 22 million barrels of Iranian crude in recent years, breached the U.S. naval blockade late last night and redirected to the Gulf of Oman. (Source: @kianmeli1/91842)
Google Earth updated imagery of Kharg Island dated April 7, 2026 — one day before the initial ceasefire of the 2026 Iran War — revealing military and dual-use sites. (Source: @shin_persian/9771)

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Baqaei declared the international justice system has failed to hold Israel accountable for its crimes in Gaza, citing the normalization of U.S.-Israeli crimes such as the Lamerd attack. (Source: @presstv/206500)

Debris from a THAAD interceptor missile was found in western Jordan months ago; the two THAAD batteries in Israel have not engaged any Iranian ballistic missiles recently because the IRGC has not fired ballistic missiles at Israel in this period. (Source: @kianmeli1/91852)

The IRGC-backed 'Islamic Resistance in Iraq' warned against 'Zionist-American plots' intended to drag Iraq into internal and external crises after denying involvement in the Saudi pipeline attack. (Source: @shin_persian/9776)

Israeli police announced the death of Yamam counter-terrorism unit fighter Itay Person, 23, whose body was found on a Haifa beach after he went missing; circumstances are under investigation. (Source: @New_security8200/203775)

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Baqaei asserted the international justice system has fundamental issues if it cannot take measures against U.S.-Israeli war crimes, specifically referencing crimes in Gaza. (Source: @presstv/206500)
Artillery shelling was reported in Al-Mansouri, southern Lebanon, with live map tracking indicating ongoing fire. (Source: @redlinkleb/42451)
Warplanes were observed flying southward over southern Lebanon, per live map tracking. (Source: @redlinkleb/42408)

Iraq closed the Shalamcheh, Sheeb, and Mandali border crossings with Iran from morning until further notice, halting all goods and passenger movement, per Khuzestan's deputy governor citing Iraqi officials. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/80749)
The Iraqi Prime Minister's office approved Iran's request for a joint investigation into drone launch platforms discovered near the Iraqi-Iranian border strip. (Source: @naya_foriraq/90309)
Saudi Arabia confirmed via Foreign Ministry statement that drones targeting the East-West pipeline originated from Iraq. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/7076)

The IRGC-backed 'Islamic Resistance in Iraq' officially denied targeting vital Saudi facilities last Friday, calling the allegation an 'honor we do not claim' and criticizing the Iraqi government for believing claims without evidence. (Source: @shin_persian/9776)
French security sources reported Iraq discovered drone launch pads near the Iranian border. (Source: @kianmeli1/91853)
A high-level Iraqi security committee arrived at the Shalamcheh border crossing to investigate 'violations.' (Source: @naya_foriraq/90303)
Basra International Airport suspended all flights to and from Iran until further notice. (Source: @mamlekate/104457)

Bahrain announced it will not participate in any joint meetings with Iranian representatives until full diplomatic relations are restored, demanding cessation of attacks, compensation, respect for sovereignty, and legal dispute resolution. (Source: @SharghDaily/183319)
Yemen's Transport Ministry reported 73 ships transited the Bab al-Mandab Strait in 48 hours, equaling 98.6% of the pre-Houthi blockade average. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/391142)

Yemen's Deputy Foreign Minister accused the Saudi regime of seeking to intimidate and mislead the international community, reaffirming Sanaa's commitment to international navigation safety. (Source: @naya_foriraq/90305)
Yemeni Armed Forces drones and snipers targeted IRGC-backed Houthi gatherings, barracks, positions, vehicles, and personnel across several fronts. (Source: @shin_persian/9767)
Iran's President Pezeshkian met with UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed on the sidelines of the BRICS summit. (Source: @asafroz/53358)
Bloomberg reported the surge in oil, gas, and diesel prices is forcing central banks and governments to reassess the economic impact of the Iran and Ukraine wars. (Source: @kianmeli1/91840)

Iran claims a Hormuz transit agreement with Oman will be signed Monday in Muscat with Arab Gulf states present, including countries whose territory was used by the U.S. for attacks on Iran. (Source: @mamlekate/104458)

sections.threat_assessment: The closure of Iraq-Iran border crossings marks a significant escalation in Iraqi-Iranian tensions, directly linked to Saudi accusations of Iranian-backed militia attacks on critical energy infrastructure. Iran's acquisition of Chinese satellite intelligence for strikes on U.S. positions in Jordan indicates deepening Sino-Iranian military cooperation and a heightened threat to U.S. forces in the region. The Saravan clashes reveal persistent internal security challenges for Iran along its southeastern frontier. The sanctioned tanker's successful blockade run demonstrates Iran's evolving sanctions evasion capabilities. Collectively, these developments suggest a multi-axis pressure campaign against Iran met with asymmetric responses across maritime, land, and intelligence domains.
sections.regional_response: Gulf states are diverging: Bahrain is diplomatically isolating Iran, while Oman hosts a Hormuz transit agreement involving Arab states that host U.S. forces. Saudi Arabia is leveraging the pipeline attack to pressure Iraq into action against Iranian-backed groups. Yemen's Houthis face continued Yemeni government drone and sniper operations, yet Red Sea shipping has nearly returned to pre-blockade levels. The UAE engages Iran diplomatically at BRICS. Iraq is caught between investigating border violations and managing militia denials. The region is fragmenting into competing security architectures.
sections.intelligence_notes: The appearance of THAAD debris in Jordan without recent Iranian ballistic missile launches at Israel suggests either unreported interceptions or training activity. The Islamic Resistance in Iraq's denial of the pipeline attack — framing it as an 'honor we do not claim' — follows a pattern of plausible deniability for Iranian proxies. The Google Earth imagery update of Kharg Island dated April 7, 2026, one day before a reported ceasefire, may indicate post-conflict damage assessment. The convergence of Chinese satellite support, BRICS financial integration efforts, and Hormuz diplomatic initiatives points to a coordinated Iranian strategy to internationalize its security and economic resilience.
